lastCompletedStory.title: Migrate integration sleeps to waitForCondition (group C: plan-runner-pane-spawn, orch-recycle-watch, orch-recycle-pid-resolve)

nextStoryContext: US-004 migrated all 13 Bun.sleepSync sites in the group-C files (6 in plan-runner-pane-spawn.test.ts, 5 in orch-recycle-watch.test.ts, 2 in orch-recycle-pid-resolve.test.ts) to waitForCondition, closing the sequential US-002/US-003/US-004 migration arc for this PRD's named groups A/B/C. Two shapes: (1) simple settle-after-mutation sites reused the existing group-A/B-style local isPaneAlive(id) (display-message '#{pane_dead}' probe) / has-session predicates, same pattern, no new helper needed. (2) orch-recycle-watch.test.ts and orch-recycle-pid-resolve.test.ts had ALREADY hand-rolled their OWN bounded while(Date.now()<deadline){...; Bun.sleepSync(n);} poll loops around pgrep/ps/readFileSync/process.kill(pid,0) checks, predating waitForCondition's introduction (US-001/CAM-62) -- these were collapsed by moving the loop body's success-detection into a waitForCondition predicate that mutates an outer-scope `let` (e.g. `newUUID`, `found`) on match and returns true/false, then reading the mutated variable after the await; call sites that asserted a boolean ('fakeclaudeRunning', 'childExited') keep that contract via a `try { await waitForCondition(...); x = true } catch { /* leave x false */ }` wrapper so the original expect(...).toBe(true) assertions are unchanged. waitForChildViaPs (orch-recycle-pid-resolve.test.ts) became async, now returns Promise<number|null> instead of blocking synchronously via its own internal Bun.sleepSync loop. One new pollable condition specific to this group: proving a just-spawned background watcher subprocess (`bun index.ts orch-recycle-watch`) is actually scheduled in the OS process table (pgrep -f 'orch-recycle-watch') before arming the marker file it watches for, replacing a blind 200ms 'let it start' sleep with a real existence check. All 13 sites had a genuine pollable condition; zero bare-sleep tracker-ref suppressions were needed anywhere in this group. Verified real (not faked): `bun test test/integration/plan-runner-pane-spawn.test.ts test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts test/integration/orch-recycle-pid-resolve.test.ts` -> 5 pass / 0 fail; full `bun test` -> 4591 pass / 0 fail; full `bun run check:all` -> exit 0, all 12 gates ok (file-size, coverage, debt-markers, dead-code, dup all clean, no ratchet raise needed). Post-migration `bun scripts/check-test-sleeps.ts` confirms zero remaining hits in all three group-C files; remaining ~55+ un-suppressed violations are scattered across test/integration/plan-runner-target-obey.test.ts, ensure-worker-pane-selfheal.test.ts, sendkeys-submit.test.ts, plan-runner-no-prd.test.ts, test/supervisor/plan/*, test/ui/init-setup-screen-keys.test.ts, and test/helpers/flush-ink.ts:22 -- none of these were named in this PRD's groups A/B/C scope (per the US-004 notes field, groups A/B/C only enumerate the 9 files covered by US-002/003/004), so they are explicitly out of scope for this story. A later story in this PRD (if any remain) or a follow-up issue should either migrate those remaining sites or same-line tracker-ref-suppress them before check-test-sleeps.ts can be wired into check:all/GATES (per the US-001 patterns.md bullet, the scanner is deliberately still un-wired).

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed Bun.spawn's Subprocess.exited is an async-only Promise (no synchronous liveness-poll primitive), and Bun.spawnSync blocks and returns a snapshot SyncSubprocess with no way to re-poll a live handle. This validates this story's approach: for cross-process liveness (a bash-wrapper-forked child, a tmux-respawned pane, or a `bun index.ts orch-recycle-watch` background subprocess not held as a single Bun Subprocess handle across the whole test), polling external process-table introspection (pgrep/ps via spawnSync) inside a waitForCondition predicate is the correct idiom -- Bun itself provides no sync subprocess-liveness API that would substitute for it here.
